questions.question: Aerated drinks such as soda water contain which gas as solute?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Carbon dioxide.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Aerated drinks such as soda water contain **carbon dioxide** as the solute.
 
• When carbon dioxide is dissolved in water, it forms **carbonic acid**, giving the drink a tangy taste.
 
• Carbon dioxide is responsible for the fizz in soda due to its release when pressure is reduced (like when a bottle is opened).
 
• Carbon dioxide is** non-toxic** and gives carbonated drinks their characteristic effervescence.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Aeration Process**: Aeration is the process of dissolving gases like carbon dioxide into liquid under pressure, which increases the solubility of the gas in the liquid.
 
• **Carbonic Acid**: When carbon dioxide dissolves in water, it forms a weak acid called carbonic acid (H₂CO₃), which contributes to the slight sour taste of carbonated beverages.
 
• **Effervescence**: This refers to the bubbles formed by the release of carbon dioxide when the pressure is reduced. In aerated drinks, this release occurs when a bottle or can is opened.
 
• **Carbonation**: The process of dissolving carbon dioxide into a liquid, typically under high pressure, to create fizzy drinks like soda water, soft drinks, and sparkling water.

questions.question: When is the Constitution Day celebrated in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** 26th November.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Constitution Day**, also known as **Samvidhan Divas**, is celebrated in India on **26th November** every year.
 
• It marks the day in 1949 when the **Constituent Assembly of India adopted the Constitution**, which came into effect on 26th January 1950.
 
• The day is observed to honor the architects of the Indian Constitution, especially Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, the chairman of the Drafting Committee.
 
• Constitution Day was **first celebrated in 2015 to commemorate the 125th birth anniversary of Dr. B.R. Ambedkar.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Adoption of the Constitution**: The Constitution of India was adopted on 26th November 1949 but came into effect on 26th January 1950, a day now celebrated as Republic Day.
 
• **Constitution of India**: It is the supreme law of India, providing the framework that defines the fundamental political principles, establishes the structure, procedures, and duties of government institutions, and outlines the rights and duties of citizens.
 
• **Drafting Committee**: The Constitution was drafted by the Constituent Assembly, and Dr. B.R. Ambedkar was the chairman of the Drafting Committee. The drafting process took nearly three years to complete.
 
• **Significance of Constitution Day**: It serves as a reminder of the values enshrined in the Constitution, such as justice, liberty, equality, and fraternity, and reinforces the importance of civic responsibilities among citizens.

questions.question: The ratio of two numbers is 5 ∶ 3 and their sum is 560. Find the value of the smaller of the two numbers.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The ratio of two numbers = 5 ∶ 3

Their sum = 560

**Formula Used:**

Let the two numbers be 5x and 3x.

Sum of the numbers = 5x + 3x = 8x

Given sum = 560

**Calculation:**

5x + 3x = 560

⇒ 8x = 560

⇒ x = 560 / 8

⇒ x = 70

Smaller number = 3x

⇒ 3 × 70

⇒ 210

**The value of the smaller of the two numbers is 210.**

questions.question: In Aditya - L1, the first Indian mission to study the Sun, what does L1 stand for?

__
 
• In Aditya-L1, the first Indian mission to study the Sun, **L1** stands for **Lagrange point 1**.
 
• L1 in Aditya-L1 stands for **Lagrange point 1**, a stable point in space located between the Earth and the Sun, about 1.5 million kilometers from Earth.
 
• **Reason for Location**
 
 
• **Stable position**: The gravitational forces of the Earth and Sun balance out, allowing the spacecraft to maintain a steady orbit.
 
• **Continuous viewing**: The spacecraft can continuously observe the Sun without interruptions from eclipses or occultations.

• The mission has a projected life of **five years**.
 
• **Payloads**:
 
 
• **Solar Ultraviolet Imaging Telescope (SUIT)**: Captures images of the Sun's photosphere and chromosphere.
 
• **L1 Orbiting X-ray Spectrometer (HEL1OS)**: Studies X-ray flares from the Sun.
 
• **Magnetometer**: Measures interplanetary magnetic fields at L1.

questions.question: The upward and downward growth of shoots and roots, respectively, in response to the pull of earth or gravity, is called:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** geotropism.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Geotropism** refers to the growth of plant organs in response to gravity. It is also known as **gravitropism**.
 
• The **shoots** of plants exhibit **negative geotropism**, meaning they grow upward, away from the pull of gravity.
 
• The **roots** exhibit **positive geotropism**, growing downward, in the direction of the gravitational pull.
 
• This growth response helps plants maintain stability and efficiently access water and nutrients from the soil.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Phototropism**: This refers to a plant's growth in response to light. Shoots typically exhibit positive phototropism, growing towards light sources, while roots generally exhibit negative phototropism, growing away from light.
 
• **Chemotropism**: It refers to a plant's growth response to chemical stimuli. For example, the growth of pollen tubes toward ovules during fertilization is chemotropic.
 
• **Hydrotropism**: This refers to a plant's growth in response to moisture. Roots generally exhibit positive hydrotropism, growing towards areas with higher water concentration.
 
• **Importance of Geotropism**: Geotropism is essential for plant orientation and resource acquisition, ensuring that roots grow towards nutrients and shoots grow towards sunlight for photosynthesis.

questions.question: Which among the following micronutrients is essential for the normal functioning of the thyroid gland?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Iodine.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Iodine** is a crucial micronutrient required for the normal functioning of the **thyroid gland**.
 
• The thyroid gland uses iodine to produce the hormones **thyroxine (T4)** and **triiodothyronine (T3)**, which regulate various metabolic processes in the body.
 
• A deficiency of iodine can lead to thyroid-related disorders such as **goiter** (enlarged thyroid gland) and **hypothyroidism** (reduced production of thyroid hormones).
 
• Iodized salt and iodine-rich foods like seafood, dairy products, and eggs are important dietary sources of this essential nutrient.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Thyroid Gland**: It is a butterfly-shaped gland located in the neck. It produces hormones that regulate metabolism, energy production, and body temperature.
 
• **Thyroid Hormones**: The two main thyroid hormones, thyroxine (T4) and triiodothyronine (T3), play a key role in controlling the body's metabolic rate, heart function, and development.
 
• **Iodine Deficiency Disorders (IDDs)**: Lack of iodine in the diet can cause conditions such as goiter, cretinism (in children), and hypothyroidism. Severe iodine deficiency during pregnancy can lead to developmental delays in children.
 
• **Prevention**: Iodized salt is a simple and effective way to prevent iodine deficiency, ensuring the normal functioning of the thyroid gland and preventing IDDs.

questions.question: The inner walls of the small intestine have thousands of finger-like outgrowths. These are called:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** villi.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The inner walls of the small intestine are lined with thousands of tiny, finger-like projections called **villi**.
 
• Villi increase the surface area of the intestinal lining, enhancing **nutrient absorption from digested food.**
 
• Each villus contains **capillaries and lacteals (lymphatic vessels)**, which help **transport absorbed nutrients and fats to the bloodstream.**
 
• The presence of villi is crucial for efficient digestion and absorption, playing **a significant role in overall nutrient uptake in the body.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Structure of Villi**: Each villus is approximately 0.5-1.5 mm in length and is covered with epithelial cells called enterocytes, which are involved in nutrient absorption.
 
• **Microvilli**: On the surface of each villus, there are even smaller projections called microvilli that form a brush border, further increasing the absorptive surface area.
 
• **Digestive Process**: As food passes through the small intestine, nutrients are broken down and absorbed into the bloodstream through the villi, which is essential for providing energy and nutrients to the body.
 
• **Disorders Related to Villi**: Conditions such as celiac disease can damage villi, leading to malabsorption of nutrients and various gastrointestinal symptoms.

**Calculation:**

1. Identify the midpoint of each class interval.

2. Plot these midpoints on the x-axis.

3. Plot the corresponding frequencies on the y-axis.

4. Connect the points with straight lines.

**The correct answer is option 1.**

questions.question: Find the value of sin ({5 pi over 3}).
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Convert the radian angle to degrees: 5π/3 = 5 × 60° = **300°**.

300° lies in the **IV Quadrant**, where the sine function is **negative**.

The reference angle is 360° − 300° = **60°**.

sin(300°) = −sin(60°) = **−√3/2**.

**∴ The correct answer is −√3/2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Angle θ = 5π/3

**Formula Used:** sin(2π − α) = −sin(α)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1166cd1e61c3bf942b8cd9cfeafc7a28e9bd81b5bad811e453d354ac59067220.png] 

⇒ θ = 5π/3 = 5 × (180°/3) = 300°

⇒ sin(300°) = sin(360° − 60°)

⇒ Using the reduction identity sin(360° − A) = −sin A

⇒ sin(300°) = −sin(60°)

⇒ We know that sin(60°) = √3/2

⇒ sin(300°) = −√3/2

**∴ The correct answer is −√3/2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

ASTC Rule (All Silver Tea Cups)

It determines the sign of trigonometric ratios: **Quadrant I** (All positive), **Quadrant II** (Sine/Cosec positive), **Quadrant III** (Tan/Cot positive), **Quadrant IV** (Cos/Sec positive).

Periodicity of Sine

Sine is a periodic function with a period of 2π. Thus, sin(2nπ + θ) = sin θ for any integer n.

Reference Angle

The acute angle α that the terminal side makes with the x-axis. In Quadrant IV, α = 360° − θ or 2π − θ.</p

questions.question: In the context of climate change, what is the full form of GHGs?

questions.question: A is twice as fast as B and B is thrice as fast as C. The journey covered by C in 54 minutes will be covered by A in how many minutes?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A is twice as fast as B and B is thrice as fast as C.

Journey covered by C in 54 minutes.

**Formula Used:**

Time taken by A = (Speed of C / Speed of A) × Time taken by C

**Calculation:**

Speed of B = 3 × Speed of C

Speed of A = 2 × Speed of B = 2 × 3 × Speed of C = 6 × Speed of C

Time taken by A = (Speed of C / Speed of A) × Time taken by C

Time taken by A = (Speed of C / 6 × Speed of C) × 54

Time taken by A = (1/6) × 54

⇒ Time taken by A = 9 minutes

**The correct answer is 9 minutes.**

questions.question: Kishore plans to tile his kitchen floor with square tiles. Each side of the tile is 10 cm. The kitchen is 2.4 m long and 1.6 m wide. How many tiles will Kishore need?

Area of one tile = Side × Side

questions.question: Raju is standing away from Karthik at a distance of 300 m. Raju starts running and Karthik chases him. Raju and Karthik run at the rate of 10 km and 12 km per hour respectively. What is the distance between them after 6 minutes?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

**Relative Speed** = 12 − 10 = 2 km/hr.

**Distance reduced** in 6 min = Speed × Time = 2 × (6/60) km = 0.2 km = 200 m.

**Final distance** = Initial distance − Distance reduced = 300 − 200 = 100 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 100 m.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of **Raju** = 10 km/hr

Speed of **Karthik** = 12 km/hr

Initial gap = 300 m

Time = 6 minutes

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/30db52042216499ad3f9f489cef969ac532da54525940d5b0ffd7d32bf30fceb.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Speed of Raju in m/min = 10 × (1000/60) = 500/3 m/min

⇒ Speed of Karthik in m/min = 12 × (1000/60) = 200 m/min

⇒ Distance covered by Raju in 6 min = (500/3) × 6 = 1000 m

⇒ Distance covered by Karthik in 6 min = 200 × 6 = 1200 m

⇒ Total distance of Raju from starting point = 300 + 1000 = 1300 m

⇒ Final distance between them = 1300 − 1200 = 100 m

**∴ The correct answer is 100 m.**

**__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed (Same Direction)
